request.system:
You are a senior QA engineer studying a voice agent before testing it.
Read everything you are given about the agent and list, using only what the text supports:
- intents: the jobs callers can ask it to do (short snake_case ids like place_order), with the tools each job uses.
- slots: the details it must collect from the caller, with a made-up example value.
- rules: every instruction or business rule it must follow, one per item, ids R1, R2, ... in order.
  kind: must (it has to do this), must_not (it must never do this), escalate (when to hand over), fact (a fact
  it may state, like a price).
- workflows: the steps of each job in order.
- unclear: things a tester would need to know that the text does not say.
Do not invent rules the text does not contain.

messages.content:
Agent: Pipecat food ordering (open source). Pipecat Flows' pizza and sushi ordering agent behind a Twilio-style phone line, with an order API and database.
Domain: food-ordering. Languages: en.

The agent's own instructions (its system prompt):
<<<
You are an order-taking assistant. You must ALWAYS use the available functions to progress the
conversation. This is a phone conversation and your responses will be converted to audio. Keep the
conversation friendly, casual, and polite. Avoid outputting special characters and emojis.

Step 1: Ask the user if they want pizza or sushi, and wait for them to use a function to choose. Start
off by greeting them. Be friendly and casual; you're taking an order for food over the phone.

Step 2 (pizza): You are handling a pizza order. Use select_pizza_order when the user specifies both size
AND type. Pricing: Small $10, Medium $15, Large $20.

Step 2 (sushi): You are handling a sushi order. Use select_sushi_order when the user specifies both count
AND type. Pricing: $8 per roll.

Step 3: Read back the complete order details to the user and ask if they want anything else or if they
want to make changes. Use complete_order when the user confirms that the order is correct and no changes
are needed (this sends the order to the restaurant with place_order). Use revise_order if they want to
change something. Be friendly and clear when reading back the order details.

Step 4: Thank the user for their order and end the conversation politely and concisely.
>>>

Business rules the agent must follow:
Tony's is a takeaway that sells pizza (small $10, medium $15, large $20; pepperoni, cheese, supreme or
vegetarian) and sushi rolls ($8 each; california, spicy tuna, rainbow or dragon, 1 to 10 rolls).
The agent takes one order per call, reads it back, and places it only after the caller confirms.
Delivery takes about 30 minutes. It has no other information (no other menu items, opening hours,
allergens or deals) and should say so rather than guess.

Tools the agent calls (Vocto sees every call and can make one fail on purpose):
- place_order (write): Sends the confirmed order to the restaurant.
- delivery_estimate (read): When the food will arrive.

Database checks Vocto can run after a call (what was really saved):
- orders_for_test: Orders placed during this call. Columns: id, food, size, pizza_type, count, roll_type, price, status.

Tests that already exist (don't write these again):
- pipecat-food.delivery-time: Caller asks how long delivery takes
- pipecat-food.order-pizza: Caller orders a large pepperoni pizza
- pipecat-food.order-sushi: Caller orders two spicy tuna rolls
- pipecat-food.order-system-down: The order system fails and the agent must say so
- pipecat-food.simulated-order: Caller orders in their own words and changes the size once
